newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain option volatilities leap after share gains.
newsitem.headline: Spain option volatilities leap after share gains.

text.p: Profit-protection anxiety after breathtaking Spanish share market gains is driving share option volatilities in the country to historic highs.
Implied volatility of June Ibex options hit a record high on Thursday at 34 percent, while for September options it was trading at around 27.5 percent.
Implied volatility, which rises as expectations of sharp moves grow, has averaged just 17 percent over the last 100 days.

Analysts said the reasons were clear. Investors are anxious to protect huge piles of cash earned on the Spanish blue-chip share index, after the Ibex-35 soared 25 percent so far this year to nearly 6,440.

"On the one hand, there is the activity of end users who are looking for a hedge against possible market declines with puts and are not directly selling the bourse for fear they will lose on a big rebound. Or they are using calls to overweight portfolios without buying," said Alex Matitia, derivatives director at ODDO brokerage in Madrid.
The chief of derivatives at another Spanish financial institution agreed there was some heavy demand for hedging to lock in investors' already sizeable profitable.
"There is great demand for put options in search of a hedge after the new levels reached," he said.
"Funds have earned a lot of money in recent months and it doesn't bother them to dedicate part of them to finance hedging through options, even though prices are exploding," he added.

On Wednesday, the bourse shed 2.3 percent, fuelling anxiety and pushing short-term option volatilities to near 34 percent, beyond former peaks near 30 percent reached in the wake of Spanish general elections in March, 1996.

"People are in the market and having reached certain earnings levels, given the sharp rise in the bourse and the possibility of turbulence like yesterday, it's logical that people are in derivatives," a fund manager said.
In addition, derivatives professionals are also driving volatilities prices in expectations of sharp moves ahead.

"In addition to hedging, market professionals are not betting on where the market will go, but how much it will move...The strategies are varied (straddles, strangles) but the result is the same -- a demand for options," Matitia said.
